item.title: Self-Hosted Audio DSP & Room Correction: CamillaDSP vs BruteFIR vs LSP Plugins
item.description:
Introduction

If you’ve ever set up a home audio system only to find that the bass response is muddy, the treble is harsh, or the stereo imaging is smeared by room reflections, you’ve encountered the fundamental challenge of room acoustics. Professional studios spend thousands on acoustic treatment, but for the rest of us, Digital Signal Processing (DSP) offers a software-based solution. By applying precise digital filters to your audio signal, you can correct for room modes, speaker non-linearities, and crossover issues — all from a $35 Raspberry Pi.

item.title: Self-Hosted MIDI Network Routing: rtpmidid vs QmidiNet vs jack-matchmaker
item.description:
MIDI Over IP: Why Network Your Instruments?

MIDI has been the universal language of electronic music since 1983, but traditional 5-pin DIN cables limit you to 16 channels over 15 meters. In a modern home studio or multi-room setup, you want to connect a keyboard in the living room to a synthesizer rack in the basement, or route MIDI from a DAW on your desktop to a Raspberry Pi running a software synth by the speakers.
